title: C. elegans survival assays for nucleotide excision repair analysis
author: van der Woude, Lans

steps.title: Prepare NGM agar plates
steps.instruction: Make NGM agar medium, add supplements, dispense into plates, and store them ready for C. elegans culture.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 3 g NaCl, 7.5 g casein digest, and 17 g agar into a 2 L autoclavable glass bottle; add 1000 mL double‑distilled water (ddH₂O).
Autoclave the bottle for 20 min at 121 °C (ensure the cap is loosened before autoclaving).
Air‑cool the autoclaved bottle to 55 °C and shake to obtain a homogeneous mixture.

Add 25 mL 1 M KPO₄ buffer (pH 6.0), 1 mL 1 M MgSO₄, 1 mL 1 M CaCl₂, and 1 mL 5 mg/mL cholesterol (ethanol stock) to the cooled medium. Note: the KPO₄, MgSO₄, and CaCl₂ solutions must also be autoclaved for 20 min and air‑cooled to 20‑22 °C before use; the cholesterol solution is already sterile.
Optional: add an antibiotic to the NGM (use ampicillin‑resistant OP50 or HT115(DE3) bacteria as food). Do not use puromycin or G418, which are toxic to C. elegans.
Optional: instead of air‑cooling, place the bottle in a water bath or incubator set to 55 °C, which is convenient when preparing multiple bottles.

Dispense the NGM into Petri dishes: ~10 mL per 90 mm plate or ~5 mL per 60 mm plate, using a peristaltic pump (or pour by hand with a glass flask equipped with a pouring ring if a pump is unavailable).
Let the plates solidify at 20‑22 °C for 2–3 days to allow contaminant detection and excess moisture evaporation.
If plates are needed immediately, store them upside down at 20‑22 °C; for longer‑term storage (up to 3 weeks) keep them upside down at 4 °C. Prevent drying by storing plates in an airtight container.

steps.title: Repeat assays and analyze statistics
steps.instruction: Perform each survival experiment at least three independent times and assess significance: use a standard t‑test for two‑strain comparisons or one‑way ANOVA for multiple strains.

description: In order to perform UV survival assays with Caenorhabditis elegans, the animal needs to be cultured and maintained. We therefore first describe basic culturing and maintenance of this animal. C. elegans is commonly maintained on Nematode Growth Medium (NGM) agar plates using Escherichia coli strain OP50 as a food source (Brenner, 1974). In our survival assays, we also use HT115(DE3) E. coli as food source, as these bacteria form a thinner lawn than OP50 and therefore block less UV light (Lans et al., 2010). Additional information about C. elegans as model organism, its biology and laboratory techniques can be found on the online resource www.wormbook.org (Girard et al., 2007; Stiernagle, 2006). It is important to feed C. elegans ample food before the survival assays start, such that the animals are minimally stressed. Each survival assay needs to start with sufficient culture plates containing well-fed adult animals.
